Frequency Chart of pitch types for the last 10 years. (most frequent pitches in 2015 all the way up to 2025) 
```{r}
BBstats1 <- BBstats %>% filter(game_type %in% c("R", "D", "L", "W")) %>% 
  filter(pitch_name %in% c("Slurve" , "Knuckle Curve", "Split-Finger", "Curveball" , "Cutter" , "Sweeper", "Changeup" , "Slider" , "Sinker", "4-Seam Fastball")) %>% 
  filter(game_year %in% c(2015, 2018, 2021, 2023, 2025)) %>%
  group_by(game_year, pitch_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Using a function to build a plot for every year instead of doing facet wrap because its easier to view this way 
pitch_freq_plot <- function(data, year) {
  data %>%
    filter(game_year == year) %>%
    mutate(pitch_name = reorder(pitch_name, -count)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = pitch_name, y = count, fill = pitch_name)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_classic() + 
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),  # y instead of x now
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Pitch Type Frequency —", year),
      x = "Pitch Type",
      y = "Count"
    )
}

plot_2015 <- pitch_freq_plot(BBstats1, 2015)
plot_2018 <- pitch_freq_plot(BBstats1, 2018)
plot_2021 <- pitch_freq_plot(BBstats1, 2021)
plot_2023 <- pitch_freq_plot(BBstats1, 2023)
plot_2025 <- pitch_freq_plot(BBstats1, 2025)
plot_2015
plot_2018
plot_2021
plot_2023
plot_2025

```


Build a Breaking ball vector then calculate the magnitude and observe its changes over the last 10 years 
```{r}
BBstats_break <- BBstats %>% 
  filter(game_type %in% c("R", "D", "L", "W")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(api_break_x_arm), !is.na(api_break_z_with_gravity)) %>%
  mutate(break_magnitude = sqrt(api_break_x_arm^2 + api_break_z_with_gravity^2)) %>%
  group_by(game_year) %>%
  summarise(avg_break = mean(break_magnitude), .groups = "drop")
  
ggplot(BBstats_break, aes(x = game_year, y = avg_break)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2025, by = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Pitch Break Magnitude (2015–2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Avg Break Magnitude (ft)"
  )

cor.test(BBstats_break$game_year, BBstats_break$avg_break)
#p-value = 0.06358
# 95 percent confidence interval: -0.03626334 - 0.87396465
# cor = 0.5761448



```



Batting Average vs Launch Angle ? (Run Statistical Test, What type of correlation)?
The higher people hit the ball vs how sucessful they are 
what we expect --> people hit the ball higher and will have a lower batting average, this is because in recent years more hitters have beeing going for a home run or bust mentality, this means that they prob hit more home runs but also have a lower batting average. How can I calcualte this change over the years. 


```{r}
BBstats_angle <- BBstats %>%
  filter(game_type %in% c("R", "D", "L", "W")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(launch_angle), !is.na(estimated_ba_using_speedangle)) %>%
  group_by(game_year) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_launch_angle = mean(launch_angle),
    avg_xba = mean(estimated_ba_using_speedangle),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(BBstats_angle, aes(x = game_year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_launch_angle, color = "Avg Launch Angle"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = avg_launch_angle, color = "Avg Launch Angle"), size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_xba * 100, color = "Avg xBA (scaled)"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = avg_xba * 100, color = "Avg xBA (scaled)"), size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Avg Launch Angle (degrees)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 100, name = "Avg xBA")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2025, by = 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Avg Launch Angle" = "steelblue", "Avg xBA (scaled)" = "tomato")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(title = "Launch Angle vs Expected Batting Average (2015–2025)",
       x = "Year")


BBstats_raw <- BBstats %>%
  filter(game_type %in% c("R", "D", "L", "W")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(launch_angle), !is.na(estimated_ba_using_speedangle))
cor.test(BBstats_raw$launch_angle, BBstats_raw$estimated_ba_using_speedangle)


```

r = -0.0236 — negative direction, confirming your hypothesis directionally
p < 2.2e-16 — essentially zero, statistically bulletproof with 1.28 million observations
95% CI: (-0.0253, -0.0219) — extremely tight, meaning this negative relationship is real and not noise



```{r}
library(tidyverse)

baseball_data <- read.csv("statcast_data.csv")
head(baseball_data)
```

```{r}
# Extract the types of events that have occurred and been recorded over the past 10 years
list_of_events <- unique(baseball_data$events)
list_of_events

# Create a vector of hit events
hit_events <- c("single", "double", "triple", "home_run")

# Create a vector of non-AB events (don't count towards batting average)
non_ab_events <- c("walk", "intent_walk", "hit_by_pitch", "sac_fly", "sac_bunt", 
                   "sac_bunt_double_play", "sac_fly_double_play", "truncated_pa",
                   "catcher_interf", "game_advisory", "ejection")

# Subsetting data to only include regular season and playoff games
game_types <- unique(baseball_data$game_type)
game_types

# Vector of only regular season and playoff game types
reg_playoff <- c("R", "D", "L", "W")

# Subsetting data to only include regular season and playoff games
baseball_data <- baseball_data |>
  filter(game_type %in% reg_playoff)
```

```{r}
# Creating a dataset with only PAs that count as ABs
AB_only_data <- baseball_data |>
  # Filtering out events that do not count as an AB
  filter(!(events %in% non_ab_events))

# Creating a summary of aggregated batting average per year
BA_overall_summary <- AB_only_data |>
  group_by(game_year) |>
  # Calculate each year's average batting average
  summarize(batting_average = mean(events %in% hit_events) |> round(digits = 4))

BA_overall_summary

# Creating a scatter plot of overall batting average versus year
BA_overall_plot <- ggplot(BA_overall_summary, aes(x = game_year, y = batting_average)) +
  # Plotting the points
  geom_point(color = "salmon", size = 2) + 
  # Plotting a line of best fit
  geom_smooth(size = 0.4, method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey") +
  # Forcing the x-axis into one-year breaks
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  labs(title = "MLB Batting Average (2015-2025)",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Batting Average") +
  theme_classic()

BA_overall_plot
```

```{r}
# Computing linear regression statistics on batting average versus year
BA_linear_regression <- lm(batting_average ~ game_year, data = BA_overall_summary)
summary(BA_linear_regression)
```

```{r}
# Analyzing all types of pitches in the AB only data
unique(AB_only_data$pitch_name)

# Deducing the total number of pitches/proportion of each type from 2015-2025
pitch_count <- AB_only_data |>
  group_by(pitch_name) |>
  summarize(total = n(), prop = round(n()/nrow(AB_only_data), 3)) |>
  # Arranging in order from most common to least common pitch types
  arrange(desc(total))

print(pitch_count)

# Deducing the total percentage of pitches thrown that the 
# six most common pitches make up
common_pitches_prop <- sum(pitch_count$prop[1:6])
common_pitches_prop

# Creating a vector of the six most common pitch types
desired_pitches <- c()
for(i in 1:6){
  desired_pitches[i] <- pitch_count$pitch_name[i]
}
```

```{r}
# Creating a summary of batting average per pitch per year
BA_by_pitch_summary <- AB_only_data |>
  # Choosing the desired (six most common) pitches
  filter(pitch_name %in% desired_pitches) |>
  group_by(game_year, pitch_name) |>
  # Calculating/summarizing the batting average per pitch type
  summarize(batting_average = mean(events %in% hit_events) |> round(digits = 4))

BA_by_pitch_summary

# Plotting the batting average per pitch type
ggplot(BA_by_pitch_summary, aes(x = game_year, y = batting_average, color = pitch_name)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  geom_smooth(size = 0.6, method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "MLB Batting Average by Pitch Type (2015-2025)",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Batting Average",
       color = "Pitch Type") +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
# Filtering out data that does not have estimated/expected (xBA) batting average values

baseball_data <- rename(baseball_data, xBA = estimated_ba_using_speedangle)
 xBA_baseball_data <- baseball_data |>
   filter(!is.na(xBA))

# Creating a new column that displays TRUE if the event was a hit, FALSE otherwise
xBA_baseball_data$is_hit <- xBA_baseball_data$events %in% hit_events
  
# Summarizing the aggregated xBA versus actual BA for 2015-2025
xBA_BA_summary <- xBA_baseball_data |>
  group_by(game_year) |>
  summarize(expected_batting_average = round(mean(xBA), 4), 
            actual_batting_average = round(mean(is_hit), 4),
            # Adding an actual BA minus xBA statistic for each year
            actual_minus_expected = actual_batting_average - expected_batting_average) |>
  # Combining xBA and actual BA into one column for data visualization
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(expected_batting_average, actual_batting_average),
    names_to = "BA_Type", 
    values_to = "BA"
  )

xBA_BA_summary
```

```{r}
# Five number summary for the actual_minus_expected BA values
delta_summary <- summary(xBA_BA_summary$actual_minus_expected)
delta_summary

# Checking for statistical outlier actual_minus_expected data
Q1 <- delta_summary[2]; Q3 <- delta_summary[5]
outlier_lower_bound <- Q1 - 1.5 * (Q3 - Q1)
outlier_lower_bound

# Filtering out the 2020 outlying actual_minus_expected statistic
xBA_BA_summary <- xBA_BA_summary |>
  filter(game_year != 2020)
  
# Plotting the two types of batting averages against the year
xBA_BA_plot <- ggplot(xBA_BA_summary, aes(x = as.factor(game_year), y = BA, color = BA_Type, group = BA_Type)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "MLB Actual vs Expected Batting Average (2015-2025)",
       x = "Season", 
       y = "Batting Average",
       color = "Batting Average Type") +
  # Renaming the color labels
  scale_color_discrete(labels = c("Actual Batting Average", "Expected Batting Average")) +
  theme_classic()

xBA_BA_plot
```

```{r}
# Plotting the actual_minus_expected BA values for each year, less 2020
delta_BA_plot <- ggplot(xBA_BA_summary, aes(x = as.factor(game_year), y = actual_minus_expected)) +
  # Creating a bar chart
  geom_col(fill = "salmon", color = "salmon") +
  labs(title = "MLB Actual Batting Average minus xBA (2015-2025)",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Actual BA - xBA",) +
  theme_classic()
delta_BA_plot
```
```{r}
# Computing linear regression statistics on actual_minus_expected BA versus year
delta_BA_linear_regression <- lm(actual_minus_expected ~ game_year, data = xBA_BA_summary)
summary(delta_BA_linear_regression)
```

```{r}
# Filtering out data that does not include launch speed and launch angle
batted_ball_data <- xBA_baseball_data |>
  filter(!is.na(launch_speed) & !is.na(launch_angle))

# Creating a heatmap for launch angle versus launch speed, colored based off proportion of base hits per unit of area
batted_ball_heatmap <- ggplot(batted_ball_data, aes(x = launch_speed, y = launch_angle, z = as.numeric(is_hit))) +
  # Sizing each unit of area to be 2mph of launch speed by 5 degrees of launch angle
  stat_summary_2d(fun = mean, binwidth = c(2, 5)) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("lightyellow", "orange", "red"),
    name = "Base Hit Rate"
  ) + 
  # Adjusting coordinates to exclude outlier values
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(50, 120), ylim = c(-40, 60)) +
  labs(
    title = "Base Hit Rate by Exit Velocity and Launch Angle",
    x = "Exit Velocity (mph)",
    y = "Launch Angle (Degrees)"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank() # Removes minor gridlines for a cleaner look
  )
batted_ball_heatmap
```

```{r}
# Computing generalized linear regression statistics on batting average versus year
batted_ball_model <- glm(as.numeric(is_hit) ~ launch_speed + launch_angle + I(launch_angle^2), 
                 data = batted_ball_data, 
                 family = "binomial")
summary(batted_ball_model)
```
